prompt: Strict top-down orthographic battlemap of a small abandoned medieval village for a tabletop wargame, seen from directly above like a satellite photo: flat orthographic projection, every roof seen straight from above as a flat shape, no building walls visible, no isometric angle, no perspective, no horizon, no sky. Between 15 and 20 separate elements in total, spread over the whole map: cottages arranged loosely in a wide ring around the plaza with open ground between them; the roofless ruin of a small stone chapel; a curved low stone wall; two short hedgerows; a few trees near the map edges; a stack of barrels. Wide open dirt lanes and grassy gaps of at least two figure-widths between every element so miniatures can walk between them. A round stone well in a small open plaza at the exact center of the map. No people, no creatures, no text, no labels, no letters, no grid, no frame, no border, no compass, no legend. Hand-drawn fantasy cartography: fine sepia and muted gold ink line art with soft transparent watercolor washes on warm cream paper, light and airy, elegant, clear readable shapes, subtle paper texture. Bright, not dark.
